1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the token against the session-bound reset record.

2.why: The same reset code cannot work for any other user because it is tied to a specific accountId in the ResetRecord.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated after password reset by marking the reset as used and clearing related session data.

4.why: The website uses HTTPS with TLS (certs/cert.pem and key.pem are loaded for Bun.serve with tls).

5.why: Reset codes are generated using randomBytes (cryptographically secure) and user data is not exposed in logs or responses.

6.why: Email messages (simulated) do not expose private user data; only mock tokens/codes are logged for testing.

7.why: User-supplied data (email, passwords) is normalized/sanitized (e.g., normalizeEmail, validPassword) and never directly interpolated into HTML/JS.

8.why: Redirect links are hardcoded to internal paths (e.g., /recovery, /login) and no user-controlled redirects exist.

9.why: Email templates are not user-controlled; the system only logs mock codes and does not render user input as HTML/scripts.

10.why: Error pages and logs explicitly avoid exposing private information (e.g., '[security] generic registered-email recovery request handled').

11.why: Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes, and no secrets are hardcoded in the source (demoAccount uses a precomputed hash).

12.why: No default credentials are present; the demoAccount requires password recovery to set a new password.

13.why: The system enforces throttling via isAllowed/failure/success functions, blocking after 5 attempts (configurable).

14.why: The application does not reveal whether a username/email exists (generic response for recovery requests).

15.why: Reset codes are random (token()), complex (base64url), and user-specific (tied to accountId in ResetRecord).
